utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. I would like to have our witness brought in, please. (The accused/witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon to the interpreters, to the court stenographers, to the Office of the Prosecutor, and to Defence counsel. Good afternoon, General Blaskic. For the public gallery, let me tell you that this is the part of the trial when the accused is testifying under oath, and this is the cross-examination which is being conducted by the Prosecution, which still has some days that are left which was calculated very carefully at the end of the morning on Friday. Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, Counsel. Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us address ourselves, General, to Prosecutor's Exhibit 456/95, and we will complete our analysis of Kiseljak. Again, General, for the record, this is the excerpt of the minutes of the Croatian Defence Council of Central Bosnia 22nd September, 1992, and under the heading dealing with the situations in municipalities, in Kiseljak, Kiseljak reads as follows: "The HVO is in complete control, however there are frequent conflicts with respect to the competencies of military and civilian authority. Almost all enterprises are working. Salaries are paid in Croatian dinars. After the conflict with the Muslims, which was staged by the leaders from Sarajevo through mujahedins, the situation is quite stable. Military HVO authority is dominant." Now, General, that particular paragraph accurately reflects the situation in Kiseljak as of the latter part of September of 1992 where the HVO was in total and complete control of that municipality; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document does describe the document, although it doesn't actually match the state of affairs there because at that time, and we saw this from other evidence, in the area of the municipality of Kiseljak, there was a war presidency which was established for the municipality of Kiseljak within the segment of civilian authority, and that war presidency functions as an entire civilian authority towards the Bosniak Muslims of Kiseljak whereas the civilian authority of the municipality of the HVO functions vis-à-vis the Croats of the municipality of Kiseljak. As for the military part, in September, there weren't any major problems. After the conflict in Duhri was taken care of and the staff of the Territorial Defence operated in the same building where the HVO staff was and the cooperation there was quite good, which can be seen from my document which is Defence Exhibit -- let me just recall that -- 395, dated the 10th of August, 1992, when, after the meeting with Dzemo Merdan, I issued an order in which, in particular in item 6, it is obvious that I am recalling an agreement and saying that it should be made possible for the members of the Territorial Defence to function. Your Honours, already on the 9th of August, that is to say, only one day after the conflict was taken care of, on the line against the Serbs we established cooperation, we defended our positions together, and we used HVO vehicles to transport army from Bilalovac to the front line against the Serbs; and the document as a whole certainly does not reflect the actual state of affairs on the territory of the municipality of Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Mr. President, to move matters along, these are two communiqués. The first is a communiqué from the Muslims of Kiseljak dated the 16th of October of 1992 calling for the legal institutions of Kiseljak to be involved in the democratic process and complaining about the usurpation of power by the HVO. Naturally, this is dated after the 22nd of September meeting where the HVO notes that they have taken full control of Kiseljak. We are not going to read these documents, Mr. President. We are simply going to offer them at this point into the record and move on to the next municipality. If I can also give the -- when the usher is finished -- provide the usher with the next document which is again another request for a meeting by the Muslims of Kiseljak and they want to meet with members of the HDZ Party to restore cooperation between the parties.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 638, 638A for the English version and 639 and 639A for the English version, and these are Prosecution Exhibits. Sorry, it's 638 and 639.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are simply placing these in the record at this time. We will move on to the next series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you changing subjects now or are you still talking about Kiseljak, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We are moving to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. All right then. These exhibits have been tendered, and are they accepted, 638 and 639; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, the next area that we would like to discuss with you is the municipality of Busovaca. During May of 1992, you made several trips to Busovaca, did you not, to meet with people like Pasko Ljubicic and Filip Filipovic and Zarko Tole; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. At the beginning of May 1992, I met Pasko Ljubicic, but it wasn't my intention to meet up with him. The commander of the HVO, Tomislav Trutina, of the municipal staff, that is, he invited me to come to Tisovac, and that is where I met Pasko Ljubicic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, for the time being, let's try to focus things here. The question was not to know whether -- why, under what conditions you met Pasko Ljubicic. If that question was asked, I think you will be able to answer it. But I think that the question was to find out whether or not, in fact, you did meet Pasko Ljubicic at the beginning of May 1992. I think the question was very simple, you can just simply answer simply, and you will see what follows in the next questions.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. If the question is whether I met Pasko Ljubicic in May, I would have responded straightaway "Yes." But, sorry, that is not the kind of interpretation I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In English, Mr. President, the question was: Did you go to Busovaca in May to meet with people like Pasko Ljubicic? So the question was: Did you go there with the purpose of meeting him? That was the English translation (sic). I don't know what the other translations were. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, let's not get into semantics here. We want to be sure that the proceedings are efficient, rapid, and balanced. All right, Mr. Kehoe, please ask the question again; that is, whether or not the witness met with Pasko Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you meet with Pasko Ljubicic and Filip Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the beginning of May 1992, I did meet Pasko Ljubicic at the reception desk of the hotel and I was sitting at a table with Colonel Filip Filipovic and I saw him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You met him. All right. So you met him then. All right. You saw him.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was this in the municipality of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you meet Zarko Tole?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Him? Around the 23rd of May, I also saw him in the municipality of Busovaca, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you Prosecutor's 208. This is a document that's dated the 10th of May, 1992, from Busovaca, and it is signed by HVO vice-president Dario Kordic and the commander of the municipal HVO headquarters in Busovaca, Ivo Brnada. I focus you to paragraphs 1, 2, and 3, General, the first paragraph reading as follows. If we can move that up a bit, Mr. Usher. Thank you. Up the other way. No, no, no. Yes, thank you, 1, 2, and 3. Up a little. Thank you. "1. The agreement between the HVO and the so-called Busovaca (Territorial Defence) on the distribution of weapons is hereby terminated, and it has been decided that the Busovaca HVO forces take over all weapons, equipment, material, as well as the barracks. "2. The town of Busovaca is to be completely blocked from all sides. "3. All paramilitary formations (the so-called TO), individuals and others are given the ultimatum to hand over all weapons in their possession by Sunday 1200 hours or to place themselves under HVO command, which includes the wearing of HVO insignia." Turn the page, please, Mr. Usher. "7. The mobilisation of all Busovaca HVO forces is to be completed. "8. The SJS/Public Security Station/ is to be taken over and the Busovaca Police Station is to be established. Until the police station is established, the only institution in Busovaca in charge of law and order which will ensure that all HVO decisions are respected is the HVO Military Police which is hereby granted overall authority." Lastly, number 11. "11. The municipal Crisis Committee is dismissed in accordance with the orders of the HVO and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and the Busovaca HVO is to take over all authority." General, the date of this document is the 10th of May, 1992, one day before you issue your order declaring that the Territorial Defence is illegal; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know which document you're talking about exactly because I haven't got that document with me, the one that I issued --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Show the witness Exhibit 502, Prosecutor's 502.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the document we discussed yesterday, General. I would have thought you would have remembered it. I apologise if we haven't done so, and you can briefly take a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yesterday was Sunday, Counsel, in case you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Counsel, for the reminder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is your order of 11 May, 1992 in response to an order by Ante Roso of 8 May, 1992. Do you have that document before you, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have the document 502. In document 502, the date is the 11th of May, and it invokes the order I got from the main staff, signed by General Ante Roso.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We've already spoken about this document already. Mr. Kehoe, please ask the question. We don't have to go through a whole discussion. We just want an answer to the question that you want to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The answer to the question was the 11th of May, which is, in fact, a day after the order signed by Dario Kordic that we just examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document which is Prosecutor's 209.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, with regard to this document of the Prosecution which I received, it is 208, I wish to say that the first time I saw this document was in this courtroom. As regards the contents of this document, I never talked to the authors. I should like to say that this document also shows what I testified to, and that is the interlinkage between the civilian and military matters, because the civilian and military authority who signed this document, it also shows --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. I interrupt the witness because there is no question on the floor. The witness is taking Prosecution time, and the Prosecutor would like to ask questions on Prosecutor's 209. If the witness wants to say additional things on this document, there will be more than adequate time on redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, General, but my time is limited, and I want to move to Prosecutor's 209.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All right. I wanted to say something about document 208 which was shown to me, and I didn't say a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You will have an opportunity to do that on redirect examination with your counsel, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to object to the way in which the questioning is going on. This is the third document that is being shown to General Blaskic and no questions are being put to him. Documents are supposed to be a basis for questions. We also had two other documents from Kiseljak that were introduced and no questions were put. These are not the closing arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is not a final argument, but we are counting the time that's going by. Let me remind you and let me remind the Prosecution as well that the Trial Chamber, under 90(G) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I must say this slowly, it has the following powers: The Trial Chamber has control over the way the examinations are made and the presentation of evidence, as well as the order in which they are going to be made so that, first, the presentation of the evidence will be effective for the ascertainment of the truth and, secondly, to avoid any useless waste of time. I want to exercise the power given to me by Rule 90(G) so that the time the Prosecutor has is not wasted with too many digressions on the part of all parties. Having said this, let me turn to Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Hayman to say that you know that the rights of the accused have been respected scrupulously, but we must also respect the possibility the Prosecutor would have to express himself. Therefore, the Prosecutor must make the connections between the documents that he thinks should be connected to one another, and if the witness feels that there must be comments about the documents, the Judge will ask him to do so. Mr. Prosecutor, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We are focusing, General, on Prosecutor's Exhibit 209, and this is a document from the HVO in Busovaca dated 22 May, 1992, signed again by Dario Kordic. On this particular document, it is signed in addition by the president of the Busovaca HVO command, Florijan Glavocevic. "1. The total blockade of the city of Busovaca established in all the directions according to the orders number 62/92 from 10 May, 1992 issued by the Busovaca HVO Municipal Command is abolished and the HVO forces in Busovaca are ordered to guard the important buildings on the municipal territory in the future, according to the order of the commander of the Busovaca HVO Municipal Command. In charge of the realisation of this order is the commander of the Busovaca HVO Municipal Command." Let us move down to 4. "4. Because the HVO of the Busovaca municipality is leading the whole organisation of life and defence of Busovaca, the Busovaca Municipal Assembly, Busovaca Municipal Executive Council, and the Busovaca Municipal Crisis Command will not do their duties any more, nor will they make any decisions, until the conditions are improved. 5. The internal organisation and the responsibilities of the governmental bodies of the Busovaca Municipal Assembly will be regulated by a special order of the Busovaca HVO Municipal Command. 7. This order will take effect immediately." Again, General, this particular document that was executed on the 22nd of May making the HVO the pre-eminent authority in Busovaca is issued at the same time the HVO is taking control of the Kiseljak municipality where you are located; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I want to comment on this document too, and I disagree that the situation in Kiseljak was the same as it was in Busovaca. My testimony, Your Honours, is based on the following, that every municipality in Central Bosnia was a state within a state, and we saw that in Kiseljak. In Busovaca, though, the agreement on the joint distribution of arms was abolished, and in Kiseljak, it was done. Further on, civilian authority in this document too deals with civilian and military matters, which is to say that the municipality, look at item 1, gives a task to the military commander at municipal level. Also in this other document, I don't know its number, but it's dated the 8th of July, 1992, the municipality of Kiseljak, which is being offered by the members of the crisis staff of the municipality of Kiseljak from the ranks of the Bosniak Muslim people, we have seen that this was a democratic offer to reach an agreement to the effect of maintaining good relations and to reach agreement on setting up a war presidency, and the war presidency had already been set up, that is to say, that this is a trick, that they are offering to meet and to set up a body which had already been set up. In Kiseljak, at least from July onwards, there was a war presidency that was functioning vis-à-vis the Bosniak Muslim people, and there was the HVO that was functioning vis-à-vis the Croat people. I'm talking about the civilian authorities. So in Busovaca, the situation was quite different from the situation in Kiseljak. These are like states within a state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let us turn our attention again to Prosecutor's Exhibit 456/95. On this document, I ask you to take a look at the situation in the Busovaca municipality as of the 22nd of September, 1992. I remind you, General, that you were in attendance at this meeting described as part of the working presidency.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I was the only member of the presidency never to have received a copy of the minutes and never to have signed it, and all the other members had signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The agenda on the front page of this on number 1, General, is the implementation of decisions to establish HVO authority. If you could turn to the situation in the Busovaca municipality, the first two sentences read as follows: "The HVO authority was set up on 9 May, 1992. The HVO is the only authority. However, the setting up of the Muslim People's Council is a concern." By the 22nd of September, when the HVO is in complete control of Kiseljak, they also note that the HVO is the only authority in Busovaca; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that the situation on the ground was as follows: I'm sure that I said that in September -- I mean, I'm talking about the civilian authorities. There was a war presidency of the municipality of Kiseljak that was functioning that consisted of Muslim Bosniak representatives, and also there was an HVO that was functioning. I don't know whether that was the situation in Busovaca in September, but later on, I know that in Busovaca also there was a war presidency of the Muslim Bosniak people and the HVO authority. There was dual authority on the ground, and I'm talking about what it was like on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, you were promoted to commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone as of the 27th of June, 1992 to assist the HVO in solidifying its authority in municipalities such as Vitez which had not fully come under the HVO umbrella; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is quite incorrect because I was not promoted on the 27th of June; I was appointed to a post, and that is not a promotion. Secondly, I had at least two priority obligations: to organise the defence at the front line and also to create armed formations. As for civilian authority, I did not cooperate with them, except for this meeting and perhaps another meeting. As regards the implementation of civilian matters, at meetings with the representatives of the SDA, et cetera, as for these forms of activity, I practically did not have any contact at all. I was not appointed as commander of the Operative Zone in order to establish civilian authority of the HVO in Central Bosnia. That was not my line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us examine the situation in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are moving now to the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us examine the situation in Vitez before you took over and then we'll examine the situation in Vitez after you took over. I ask you at this point to take a look at three Defence Exhibits, and these are Defence Exhibits 13, 14, and 15, which are Vitez municipality crisis staff meetings from the 9th of May, the 12th of May, and the 22nd of May respectively. We are not going to read all of these documents, General. I will focus your attention on various portions of these documents and ask you questions after I have focused your attention on these documents.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As regards your first question, what the situation was like in Vitez before I was appointed, I can answer that I don't know because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, there is no question on the floor at this point, so I will have to stop you at this particular juncture.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. I heard that question in your introduction. That's the kind of interpretation I got.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, examine these three documents starting with Defence Exhibit 13. We will start with Defence Exhibit 13, and I focus your attention on paragraph 9. Now, in paragraph 9, it notes -- and this is a Vitez municipal crisis staff document, minutes, signed by the president of the crisis staff, Ivan Santic: (as read) "9. It is necessary to establish up a single operative defence body, consisting of two representatives of the HVO, the Territorial Defence, and the Ministry of the Interior MUP, who will draw up the defence plans for the Vitez municipality and will take care of all activities related to defence. The operative body will consist of: the HVO Commander, the TO Commander, the head of the MUP, and two members of the HVO and TO chosen by the operative staff." Let us turn to the next document. This is the 12 May, 1992, which is Defence Exhibit 14. Again, we are going to focus on those paragraphs where -- if we can put that on there, Mr. Usher, 14? We are going to focus on those paragraphs where the TO is working together with the HVO. Let us look at number 3 and number 7: (as read) "3. The HVO police and the TO must raise discipline of the armed personnel during curfews to an acceptable level. "7. HVO and TO commanders are charged with certifying absence for work for people assigned to the HVO and TO. The conclusion is to be forwarded to enterprises. "9. It is necessary to hold a meeting with representatives of HDZ and SDA branches in local communities. The meeting is to be attended by representatives of the parties of the municipality." It is signed by again -- actually, the document is from the crisis staff commander, Ivan Santic. Then the last document is Defence 15, and that is crisis staff conclusions as of the 22nd of May, 1992, concerning a conflict that took place at the Vitez Hotel and notes: (as read) "1. Commanders of the TO and the HVO and the Chief of the Public Security Section should keep police forces in a state of readiness and, if necessary, mobilise additional carefully chosen military units for the preservation of order and peace. State of readiness should remain in force until further notice." So, General, for a time prior to your appointment as the commander of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone, the Muslims and the Croats in the Vitez municipality appeared to get along, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Muslims were doing well in terms of negotiating with Croats in Kiseljak, and at the time described in these documents, I was not in Vitez, I had not set my foot in Vitez until July, but from these documents I can say that it is clear that the civilian authorities are in command or have authority over the HVO, and the municipal crisis staffs issued direct orders to the commanders and units of both the TO and the HVO in terms of military affairs, and as we saw, the cooperation between the two was good in the Vitez municipality in the previous period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, shortly after your appointment to the position as commander of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone, the HVO began to solidify its position in Vitez in the same fashion as they solidified their positions in Kiseljak and Busovaca; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I did not deal with this issue of consolidation of Vitez at that time. Whenever I identified the most urgent problems, such as the situation in Jajce, I would go there. The only role for the -- Novi Travnik and Vitez was to send troops to -- reinforcements to Jajce so that we could defend it against attacks of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you, as a military commander, were part of the overall plan of the HVO to take over municipalities such as Kiseljak, Busovaca, and thereafter Vitez, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I never even saw such a comprehensive plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us look at and examine a few of the protests by the Muslims that were filed after, and shortly after, you took over as commander of Central Bosnia, and the first one, Mr. President, is one dated 12 July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is this a Prosecution or Defence Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is a Prosecution Exhibit, it is a new document, 640, and 640A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This document, unfortunately, is not in French, Mr. President. I would read it slowly. As I noted previously, the date is 12 July, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you going to read the entire document, or do you want to concentrate on a specific point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will concentrate on a specific point, Mr. President, if that is acceptable to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, you had better. It would be better for you to define things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ask your question, and if the witness wants to look at the entire text, then he, of course, can. But what kind of document is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular document, Mr. President, is a protest coming from the SDA Party, the Party of Democratic Party, which was the Muslim Party, against the actions of the HVO, and it is a press release, Mr. President, that speaks about a meeting of the executive board of the Vitez SDA that took place on 11 July, 1992, and in this particular document, the Muslims discuss the setting up of a coordination board for the protection of the interests of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But the focus of my attention, Mr. President, is the second-to-last paragraph, which notes as follows, General: "The Muslims of Vitez do not recognise --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please speak slowly. All right. You say that in Vitez they did not recognise -- what was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: " -- the Herceg-Bosna HVO as a body of authority and consider its decisions to be invalid. The Muslims in Vitez will respect the legally elected bodies of authority but will recognise future changes only if they are in conformity with valid laws, the decisions of the Vitez/Municipal Assembly/ and the platform of the BH State Presidency." Now, General, how long after your appointment as commander of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone was this document issued?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document was issued some 15 days after my appointment, but it is clear that the document was issued by the Party of Democratic Action, and I believe that it sent it to the civilian authorities of the Vitez municipality. It is signed by the Information Committee of the Coordinating Board for the Protection of the Interests of Muslims which then grew into the war presidency of the Vitez municipality. I was not part of the civilian authorities of the Vitez municipality, and I believe that they did correspond and that they did negotiate and make agreements, but this has nothing to do with me. I, for instance, incidentally, had set up my headquarters in the village of Kruscica, which was a majority Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may move to the next document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 641, 641A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This again, General, is a press release that emanates from the Vitez Coordinating Board for the Protection of the Interests of Muslims from a meeting dated 21 July, 1992, and I focus your attention to the subject of taxes, a matter which you discussed in your questions in response to Mr. Nobilo's questions -- excuse me, your answers in response to Mr. Nobilo's questions, and it notes that: "In respect of para-state institutions (of the HVO Government), we believe that the taxes introduced by the said institutions carry no legality, given that the required approval was not received from the Vitez / Municipal Assembly / board members. We support the introduction of certain taxes in order to fund the explicit needs arising from the circumstances of war, but it is imperative that they be introduced through the legal bodies of the authorities and on the principles of budgetary expenditure." Now, General, when the HVO issued these particular taxes, they imposed these taxes on Muslims as well as on Croats, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not a member of any of the boards which were adopting these decisions, but if you just show me a document, I can comment on it, but from what I know, taxes were collected in such a way that the HVO collected it from the Croats and then the coordinating board, committee, or the war presidency which consisted of Bosniak Muslims, collected both taxes and other contributions from the Muslims and which can be seen from the document which reflects this tax collection practice, and this shows that I have no influence in tax collecting because it was the municipal government bodies which were also paying for the military structures. I was not a member of the civilian structures. I would have to read the entire document to perhaps see anything that I may have missed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was it clear to you, General, that the Muslims were unhappy about the imposition of taxes as enacted by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: One second. I thought I saw somebody in the public gallery who was making a telephone call. I wanted to be sure that security prevents that sort of incident. All right. You can continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, my question to you was: Was it clear to you that the Muslims were unhappy about the HVO's imposition of taxes?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First, if we're talking about imposing taxes, nobody -- no authority is happy if they have to pay any taxes when the whole system has collapsed, when communication had broken down. What I was talking about was the situation in the field, and we saw that from the document in respect of the Kiseljak municipality. The Croats were paying their taxes to the HVO and the Muslims to the coordinating committee or the war presidency. And then let me point out to you that duties, custom duties, had been introduced in the middle of Bosnia, and the Croats had to pay it for the benefit of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let us turn your attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 503.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, my apologies for interrupting here, but a key word for understanding this document has been interpreted as illegible. It consists of about ten letters, and I think only three are illegible. Before the words which are in brackets, Vitez HVO -- in the first paragraph, before it, there is the word "institution" and before that -- and the word before that has been called illegible, but in the Croatian original, it says, "The functioning of parallel institutions" so that P-A-R-A is legible and then the next three letters are illegible and N-I-H which is the ending, Croatian ending for "parallel," and this is what is a key word because our client here is talking about these parallel institutions and this key word was not rendered into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. If necessary, you can refer back to that when you redirect. Please continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move to Prosecutor's Exhibit 53 which is another press release from the Coordination Board for the Protection of Muslim Interests, and we are focusing on the first paragraph. The date of this press release is 10 September, 1992. Mr. Usher, if you can just pull that down just a little bit? Thank you very much. "According to the decision of the so-called Croatian Defence Council/HVO/Government of Vitez municipality ... of 3 September 1992 it has been decided that instruction in elementary and secondary schools in the territory of the municipality of Vitez / illegible words / 1992. The same decision states that the schoolbooks published in the Republic of Croatia shall be used during instruction and that the school buildings and premises should be prepared in such a way that all emblems, pictures, frescoes etc. associated with the former (Yugoslav) State, the so-called Yugoslav People's Army and its history or with people from the enemy states (Serbia, Montenegro, and the so-called Federal Republic of Yugoslavia) are removed from the school building and premises. "We hereby voice our outrage at this decision because it has been made by an illegal organ, created on the principle of a single nationality." In this particular document, General, the Muslims are upset about the unilateral institution into the schools of a curricula from the Republic of Croatia, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I listened to the interpretation very well -- I did not read the entire document -- but in listening to what you've said and the interpretation that reached me, what they're talking about is introducing the textbooks from the Republic of Croatia in order to organise a curriculum, and we're talking about September 1992 which means that it was the beginning of the new school year, and they were not able to buy the textbooks from Sarajevo because Sarajevo had been under siege and I don't believe that they had been printed. This is what shows that the municipality is dealing with issues that were supposed to be decided at the state level because the state was supposed to organise the school curriculum. But what they're talking about is removing all the emblems and the symbols of the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the JNA, which was the aggressor which was active in many parts of the territory of Bosnia. So if this translation is correct, this relates to the removal of these symbols which was supposed to have been decided by the state level. So the municipality was forced to take over the role of the state organs because the state was not able to regulate these issues at that level, municipal level, and the emblems and symbols mentioned relate to the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and as far as Serbo-Croatian language or -- the Serbo-Croatian language was the official language in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, we will read the rest then: "... we consider the structure of instruction, as conceived by the nationally exclusive HVO government of Vitez municipality, to severely harm the Muslims' national interests. We cannot interpret these actions by the illegal HVO government of Vitez municipality as anything but crude disregard of Muslims' demands to continue to live in these territories as Muslims, just as their ancestors did for centuries." Last paragraph, if we can move that up, Mr. Usher. "This is yet another example of the so-called democracy in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. We are stressing that for a long time already, the nationally exclusive HVO authorities have been gaining ground in Vitez." Now, they are upset about the HVO implementing a nationally exclusive programme into the schools, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see that the document which you're reading to me does not make mention of a programme, only the textbooks and learning aids. If the printing plant does not work in Sarajevo, I have to get the textbooks from somewhere. So maybe I'm bringing it in from the neighbouring country. The state had not regulated these issues. All our classrooms had Tito's picture on them, and after the aggression had started, these symbols were ordered removed. But what is shown here is the duality of power or maybe two parallel authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's talk about that duality of power. Again, let's go back to 456/95 and address ourselves to the situation in municipalities and now focus on Vitez. Do you have that document before you, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It says: "There is still dual authority." Again, this is as of 22 September, 1992. "There is still dual authority. There is a possibility of confrontation between the Croats and the Muslims because of the HVO's taking power." So at this juncture, the 22nd of September, the HVO has taken power in Kiseljak, has taken power in Busovaca, and is taking power, as opposed to "has taken," is taking power in Vitez; isn't that what this document reflects?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is what is stated in the document, but referring to the document of 10 September, which you have just shown me, that is what I was referring to, that there was dual power, that there was parallel authority, and this parallel authority was functioning. From the later documents, we can see that -- if you have the document of 8 July, '92, there was a war presidency in operation which was communicating with the HDZ. But I was not a member either of the war presidency or the civilian authorities, so I can only comment on what I saw on the ground and what I can see here in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is a possibility in Vitez of a confrontation, General, between the Croats and the Muslims because the HVO wants the Bosnia-Herzegovinan government out; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Whether this is so, we can see it from other documents. The potential for conflict was in several areas where the state authorities had completely collapsed and you had parallel authorities. If we were to have relied on the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you couldn't have bought a single textbook because it had just stopped functioning there. So, of course, there was a potential for conflict. For 50 years, people had no rifles in their homes, and now everybody had weapons all of a sudden. Even today, there may be 100 pounds of explosives hidden in every house there. So the potential for conflict was very much there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let us look at the area of this document, 456/95, under the observations noted in all municipalities. The next page, Mr. Usher, the next page if we could. Let us read this one area, General. "Exiled Bosnia and Herzegovina Government and its bodies with pro-Muslim policies are undesirable on our territory and their possible activity contrary to the principles of HDZ bodies shall not be tolerated." Now, that particular statement is what this take-over in Central Bosnia is all about, isn't it, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already stated that in Central Bosnia, there was dual authority functioning. We saw that from many documents. I know that parts of the BH government were also functioning in Zagreb. I also know that parts of the military authorities were functioning in Zenica, and I know that in July, August, September, even October, there were various forms of cooperation of the military authorities. It is obvious that the civilian authorities were divided, that the Croats and Muslims each had their own parts of the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, you just said, "I know that parts of the BH government were also functioning in Zagreb." Could you explain that a little?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sometime in May or perhaps in early June, I don't think that the date is absolutely essential at this point, but I can look it up later, there was a large convoy which had been abducted. This was a TO convoy with equipment and weapons, and it was travelling from Fojnica to Visoko to the main logistics base of the armed forces of the BH army in Visoko. This convoy was abducted by the Fojnica HVO. When I got involved in order to return this convoy, I met a person who worked on this, and he said that he was in communication with his office in Zagreb for the needs of the BH army in transferring weapons and equipment. I know that this office was in operation in Zagreb for quite awhile. Later on, it was attached to the Bosnian embassy in Zagreb. Since there was an embargo in force for buying weapons, this could not have been done legally, and they used their own channels. He was doing it on behalf of the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I cannot say -- his father's nickname was Hadzija, so I don't have his name right here, but I can look for it in my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just by way of clarity, General, this convoy that the Fojnica HVO took was in May of 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was in May 1992. That wasn't the first convoy. Many convoys had passed through, but this convoy was partially robbed, looted, and we had tried to bring it back to the checkpoint in Visoko. This is when this gentleman appeared to have said that he was working through his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let us just change subjects for a moment, and let us stay with this document that we have before you, Prosecutor's Exhibit 456/95. I ask you to go up one paragraph from Vitez, the situation in municipalities, and I want to discuss with you the issues in Novi Travnik. Do you see that, General? That is the first municipality discussed under the rubric "Situation in Municipalities." The first sentence notes as follows: "Novi Travnik: It is estimated that the HVO holds about 70 per cent authority while the Muslims hold about 30 per cent. The question of special purposes production has to be urgently resolved." Now, General, I want to talk to you first about this special purposes production in Novi Travnik, and that relates to the Bratsvo factory in Novi Travnik, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In Novi Travnik, there was a military factory that belonged to the former Yugoslav People's Army, and it was called BNT, Bratsvo Novi Travnik. It made various projectiles from 40 millimetres to 262 millimetres, practically all kinds of artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the HVO wanted it, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The HVO wanted, together with the Territorial Defence, for this factory to operate because, according to the doctrine of the former Yugoslav People's Army, every military factory had so-called war stocks in order to continue its production unimpeded for about six months. When the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the HVO and the TO made every effort for this quantity of stocks to be manufactured so that the problem of arming the HVO and the TO would be resolved for the needs of defending Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, how far is Novi Travnik from the front line with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not say exactly how many kilometres this is. I know where the front line against the Serbs was, but the actual kilometres, that, I cannot say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you were the commander of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone. Give us an approximation. I'm not asking you specifically. Give us a rough approximation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For three or four weeks, you were showing us with your pointer, showing us everything that you knew about that area. The Prosecutor is not asking you to indicate exactly where it was.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you're asking for an approximation, that's different. But if you're asking me how far away the front line is, I thought that I had to give a precise number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Let's not waste any time here. We're not asking for the specific number of kilometres that there were. We're just asking for approximations here. If you can't tell us, then just say that you can't tell us.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would rather say that I didn't know how far it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. That's been noted.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: But I know where the front line is, and I can still show where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's get to the crux of the matter. Mr. Kehoe, we're going to take a break soon. Do you want to ask another question or should we stop at this point? What would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I just say, General, would it be fair to say that it's between approximately 15 kilometres, Novi Travnik to the Serb front line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you see, now I'm getting a question in relation to Novi Travnik. Mr. President, with the best of intentions, if I want to answer something, the town of Novi Travnik in Bosnia is one thing and the municipality is another thing. If the question is being put to me, how far away the municipality of Novi Travnik is from the front line, there is no distance because the front line is in the municipality. But if the question relates to the town itself, I'm not from Novi Travnik. I can't say exactly. I spent very little time in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Prepare your question, and you can ask it after the break. The General will think about the number of kilometres, and then I think we will get an approximate proper answer after a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Please be seated. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, the question again: From the town of Novi Travnik to the front line against the Serbs, do you have an approximate distance for us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, possibly about 10 kilometres, a 10-kilometre distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, as we move into October of 1992, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna wanted to solidify their territorial claims by ensuring the communication routes between Central Bosnia were connected down through Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, and Prozor; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know if I got the proper interpretation. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna -- could you please repeat your question? Please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Certainly. Certainly. As we move into October, the HVO wanted to solidify their territorial claims in Central Bosnia by taking control of the communication routes that led to Central Bosnia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Would you please tell me, since the HVO name is the same for the military and the civilian part, are you asking me about the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, the military part of the HVO, so that things will be clear to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was never a member of the civilian authorities. I can give my comments, I can give you my opinion about this, but the military command of the HVO in October 1992 had a front line in Jajce of 107 kilometres, it was 107 kilometres wide, together with the Territorial Defence and the members of the HOS, and we did everything in order to survive and to defend these areas, and a special priority was to get ready for the winter and to carry out defence during the winter in this mountainous terrain of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was our preoccupation in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us stay with your statement, General. In early October of 1992, did the HVO engage in ceasefires with the VRS or the Bosnian Serb army on the front line around Jajce?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know -- as far as I know, I'm saying -- there were no ceasefires in practice, but I know, on the basis of intelligence reports, that both one and the other talked, negotiated about the establishment of a cease-fire. Negotiations were carried out by the civilian authorities of both sides, that is to say, the Croatian side and the Muslim side together against the Serbs, but it all ended by the Serbs taking Jajce on the 28th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, let me have you take a look at a document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 642, 642A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this is an order coming from the 1st Krajina Corps, which is the army, of course, as you know, of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and signed by Commander Major-General Momir Talic. Do you know General Talic, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw him on television after the Dayton Accords were signed and after the Republika Srpska was established. I never met him in person, I never saw him, I was never introduced to him, and I never communicated with him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated the 7th of October, 1992, from the command of the 1st Krajina Corps forward command post. And, Mr. President, I know this will be a little bit laborious, but I would like to go through this. This is a cease-fire and reconnection of power supply. Now, before we go into this, there was a power supply in Jajce that was of extreme importance to the army of -- or the Bosnian Serb army; isn't that right, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There are two facilities in Jajce that are of exceptional importance if we're talking about hydroelectric power plants, I think there are two, and both are of exceptional importance for anyone who has Jajce under his control, and especially for the Bosnian Serbs because the entire region of Banja Luka gets electricity from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us read this document, General. "Pursuant to the order of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska ... of 6 October 1992 regarding the cease-fire and turning on of power from the Jajce-2 hydroelectric PowerPoint, I hereby issue the following order: "1. Implement the cease-fire in the sectors of the front line near Bosanski Brod, Jajce, Bugojno, Livno, Travnik, Kupres, and in Herzegovina. The cease-fire shall come into effect on 7 October 1992 at 2400 hours. The cease-fire also means a cessation of the combat activities in Slavonski Brod, the left bank of the Sava River, and in the areas surrounding the above-mentioned towns. "2. Create conditions for the repair of the Jajce-2 hydroelectric powerplant so firing from all firearms should cease for as long as the repair is under way, for at least four hours, after which the Croatian side will reconnect the power supply for the needs of Republika Srpska. "3. After the repair has been done and the power supply reconnected for our needs, the water needed for the functioning of other powerplants should be released three hours after the electric power supply has been reconnected at the latest. "4. Prepare a prisoners exchange according to previously compiled lists. The exchange will take place on 11 October 1992 at a location agreed upon by the representatives of the parties. "5. During the cease-fire, take measures to maintain the highest possible level of order and discipline at the positions, among the units engaged in combat and those in the rear. Therefore, forbid the men to leave positions and units and to move outside the combat area. "Explain to the soldiers and officers the purpose of the cease-fire, and be ready to open fire at any time at the previously determined targets if the other side does not comply with the cease-fire agreement." Now, General, did you have many cease-fire agreements such as this executed with the Serbs during October of 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document, and I already said that I never talked to the author of this document. The only thing I know in relation to these agreements is that there were agreements at local level too and that ceasefires were being agreed upon because in Jajce the Serbs had water under their control and the Croats and the Muslims had the hydroelectric power plants under their control. However, October was the month of the heaviest fighting and of the fall of the town of Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you would agree with me, General, that the control of hydroelectric power plant, Jajce-2, was a very significant matter, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was a significant matter, certainly, but I wish to underline once again that with regard to these questions, I never took part in these discussions but I did have intelligence reports telling me that this was being done at local level. For example, on the 6th of October, I had a meeting with Colonel Sartre, the commander of the French Battalion of UNPROFOR in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, your troops were at the line in Jajce, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From Central Bosnia, that is to say, from Jajce, and there was also the TO and there was the HOS, all of us were defending Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, General, that you were unaware that your troops at the front line were told not to fire on the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. I am claiming that I never took part in these negotiations. These negotiations were carried out at municipal authority level, and probably they cooperated along their own lines with civilian authorities, perhaps even top authorities from Herceg-Bosna, but I personally did not take part in negotiations. I believe that when a cease-fire was agreed upon, and there was quite a bit of this because a lot of people were losing their lives there, that the army did receive orders to stop firing. At any rate, our objective in Jajce was to stop combat operations because we were facing two Krajina corps, the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps wanted to take Jajce, and in Jajce there were so few defenders that we sent the troops in from Central Bosnia so that they would help along those 107 kilometres of the front line, but the Serbs did take Jajce on the 28th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you do know that your soldiers were told to stop firing around the 6th or 7th of October, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was the date, I can't recall whether it was the 6th of October when they were told to stop, but if there were any negotiations anywhere, and we can see from this document that there were, certainly an attempt was made to gain time, and therefore soldiers were issued such orders. Whether this was specifically on the 6th or before that or after that, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I go back to my question, General: How many times did the HVO soldiers on the Jajce front line, how many times were they told to stop firing?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Every time when the front line was being regrouped, so to speak, in Jajce, that is to say, after heavy fighting, starting from July and all the way up to October, sometimes perhaps once a month, sometimes twice a month, in order to gather the corpses, exchange them, et cetera. That is practically what is done by all armies that clash at front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, General, at the front lines, as we look at this particular order, Prosecutor's Exhibit 642, the HVO was dealing with the Bosnian Serb army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that at the front line, the HVO, the TO, the HOS had contact with the Bosnian Serbs because somewhere we were divided by a canyon, somewhere only by a forest, in some places there were only 100 metres between them. They could call out to one another in these mutual contacts. But then the bunkers were also facing one another and the fighting was taking place and sometimes there were heavy losses during one day only; for example, there would be 70 soldiers who would lose their lives in one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, with regard to Novi Travnik, the HVO was looking for a reason to engage in a conflict in Novi Travnik so they could take the Bratstvo factory; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, there was no need for that, especially not at that time. If we are talking about October now, October 1992, the HVO had excellent cooperation, except for certain incidents, with the TO in many municipalities, and this cooperation resulted in an acknowledgement given in writing that I received from the municipality of Olovo in November and then later from Gorazde, the head of the war presidency came to thank me in Maglaj and Zavidovici. In Maglaj, it was most heavily attacked by the army of Republika Srpska. There was a commander who was a Croat and Sulejman Herceg, a Bosniak, was deputy commander in Travnik and in other places. So I did not realise that attempts were being made to take the factory although I do not preclude the possibility of the civilian authorities acting only one on behalf of that particular one, the Bosniaks only on behalf of the Bosniaks and the Croats and on behalf of the Bosniaks, but this was not binding on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, between the 19th of October and the 23rd of October, 1992, when fighting was taking place in Novi Travnik, the Serbs did not shell the HVO side, did they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Where? In which part were they not shelling? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When the conflict was taking place in October between the Muslims and the Croats in Novi Travnik, the Serbs didn't shell the HVO, did they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The HVO of Novi Travnik, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let me check this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, you were there, weren't you? You were in Novi Travnik, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, I was not in Novi Travnik. On the 19th, I was in Mostar, and, sorry, Mostar is in southern Herzegovina. I was not in Novi Travnik at all on the 19th, and on the 23rd, I was in Sarajevo at a meeting in the building of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. What was happening in Novi Travnik, I will have to check in the chronology. On the 19th of October, I was in Mostar, and on the 23rd, I was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about, General, the 20th, the 21st, and the 22nd? Were you in Novi Travnik then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was not. On the 20th, I was not in Novi Travnik. On the 21st, I was there at 4.00 in the morning, and that is the first time I came to Novi Travnik, that is, at 4.00. This was after the meeting that was held until 3.00, and it was chaired by Colonel Bob Stewart, Brigadier Andrew Cumming, and the interpreter and Captain Nick, and Dzemo Merdan. We were agreeing on a cease-fire for Novi Travnik, and we wanted combat activities to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Novi Travnik after you got there at 4.00 on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stayed until noon. In the afternoon, I returned to the Hotel Lovac or, rather, the Motel Lovac in Vitez and Kruscica, and I met with Marko Prskalo. I was getting him ready to join the commission on the cease-fire. On the 22nd of October, I was in Kiseljak in order to meet the head of the main staff of the HVO, Milivoj Petkovic, and together with him, I was supposed to attend a meeting with General Morillon in relation to preparing a meeting for Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us talk about the conflict, General. You said that on the 19th, you were down in Mostar with Bruno Stojic, and then Bruno Stojic asked you about the problems that were taking place in Novi Travnik on the 19th; do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the 19th, did you or your headquarters issue an order after the conflict broke out to block all the roads coming towards Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally did not, but I was not at headquarters, so I cannot say for sure whether any of my officers from the staff had issued such an order. But at 10.00 in the morning, I attended a meeting with Bruno Stojic in Mostar, and on that day, until I returned to Kiseljak in the evening, I did not issue any orders, nor did I receive any other information related to the events in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And I returned -- let me just say this: I returned to Kiseljak on the 19th of October, 1992 at ten past eight p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let me give you a document, and we will move through these documents quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 643, 643A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this is an order that comes from your chief of staff, Ivica Cobanac, to all municipal staffs of Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, Kiseljak, Fojnica, Gornji Vakuf, and Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could the witness be allowed to read the document before the question -- I think it's difficult --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: -- for me to read it while Mr. Kehoe is posing his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm going to read the document, Mr. President. Thank you, Counsel, for your assistance. I'm going to read the document, given the fact that we do not have a French copy at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The document is going to be read, Mr. Hayman, and the witness will answer in respect of the points in the document that he has read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the 19th of October, 1992 and it notes: "Owing to the current situation in the territory of Novi Travnik municipality, I hereby order: 1. Block all roads in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, except for the passage of units and goods of strategic importance. 2. Prohibit passage to all units, except units of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna HVO. 3. Pay special attention to communications leading toward Novi Travnik. 4. This order takes effect immediately. Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Chief of Staff, Ivica Cobanac." General, this particular order was issued immediately after the conflict began in Novi Travnik, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because as far as I know, in the early evening of the 18th of October, fighting broke out in relation to the gasoline station and the hotel in Novi Travnik, that is to say, in the evening of the 18th of October, there was a conflict already, and I know that now, and this went on the 19th and the 20th. This order was issued on the 19th. However, Mr. Cobanac was not head of the staff of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia; he was head of operations in the staff of the command for Central Bosnia. I don't know why his post has been misquoted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular blocking of all roads in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was a significant event, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I was moving through part of the TO and the HVO on my way from Mostar and back on the 19th, obviously, this order was not carried out, because I passed checkpoints without any difficulty from Kiseljak via Kresevo, Konjic, Jablanica, then Mostar, that is to say, of the HVO and of the TO and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, General Blaskic. I'm sorry for interrupting you. Sometimes I have the impression that you answer as if you're an outside witness, as if you were looking at this Novi Travnik battle somewhat from the outside. Try to help the Judges. Were you in a position of responsibility or were you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm trying to give as direct an answer as possible to the question. Perhaps I didn't understand the question very well. On the 19th, I was in Mostar while the fighting was going on. I was attending meetings, and I already said that I was not in Novi Travnik. I wasn't there on the 20th when the fighting was going on in Novi Travnik, and I wasn't there on the 18th either. I arrived only on the 21st in the morning, at 4.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You were the chief. When you had responsibilities, whether you were in Mostar or in your Operative Zone, you did have responsibilities. Reassure me, please. You're saying that you were in Mostar, so we have the impression that what was going on in your area did not concern you. Please try to help the Judges. Did that concern you or did that not concern you, this type of order? Were you or were you not aware of this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this order. Today is the first time I see this order, and also this signature is not correct or, rather, there is no signature. The post that is mentioned here, the chief of staff, that is something that Mr. Cobanac never was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, but there is the command of your zone. Otherwise, the Prosecutor could tender these documents and the Defence could answer subsequently. If the witness was not there, even though he was the commander, he doesn't seem to recognise the documents or know what was going on, I think we have to note that. We want to know actually whether you felt that you were in a position of responsibility. You were the chief, after all; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I do not understand this right or perhaps I don't have a good interpretation of this, but what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Military responsibility is what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly, as military commander of this area, I was responsible for what was going on in my zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: When roads that you are responsible for are blocked, you would know that the roads are being blocked, and you said, "Well, I was able to walk around." You speak as if you are a foreign wanderer who said, "Well, obviously, this hadn't been applied because I was able to go through. So it didn't matter." You see, I'm interested in how this trial is being conducted. I don't want to waste time. We're noting your answer, and then we will move to another area. I would ask the Prosecutor to ask the question again, this is in order to assist the Judges, because, otherwise, we really don't know what we're talking about. Roads are blocked; strategic roads are blocked in your Operative Zone, and you're either in Mostar and you don't know or you say that it wasn't carried out, "I was walking about," or at least, "I was there. Everything was fine." If that's your answer, then we will keep that as your answer, and that's all. Would you ask your question again, Mr. Kehoe, in a very specific manner?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you knew that an order had been issued by your command post to block all roads in Herceg-Bosna; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not know because I was not at my command post. I did not know, but I can explain what this order meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's it. You didn't know. You just said you didn't know. If you want to explain, you can, but don't be too detailed. I think you're simply saying that you don't know, and that's your right to say, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not know that this order was issued because I was away on a trip to Mostar, but I assume that my command issued such an order so that the conflict would be localised. On the other hand, there were roadblocks all over, on both one side and the other. But I'm saying that not a total blockade had been carried out because I passed all checkpoints without being stopped, that is to say, of the TO and of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this particular document is sent by the packet system, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document should have been sent by the packet communication, but again I have already spoken about the unreliability of the packet communication because other persons could have been involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, General, concerning your activities on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 644, 644A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, is this your order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is my report of 12.07 on 20th October, 1992. This is not an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise. Your report. So you're having acknowledged that it is your report, and it is a report on the situation in Novi Travnik and Travnik as of 12.07, and it goes to Mate Boban, Bruno Stojic, and Milivoj Petkovic, and all Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna Municipal Staffs. "1. The situation in Novi Travnik is deteriorating. Territorial Defence forces are fiercely shelling the entire town area using 120 millimetre Howitzers, 120 millimetre mortars, 20/3 PAT/ anti-aircraft guns/ and other weapons. "Rasim Delic, the Commander of (Territorial Defence) units from Visoko, and the (Territorial Defence) Supreme Command Staff from Sarajevo are in charge of the operation. Zejnil Delalic, the commander of (Tactical Group) 1, who is providing logistic support and sending reinforcements from Gornji Vakuf and Bugojno, is cooperating with them. "The probable objective of the TO forces in Novi Travnik is to completely destroy and drive HVO forces from the town, and then do the same in Travnik and other places in the entire zone of responsibility. "Everything is well-planned and there is good coordination, especially with the TO forces from Konjic, which are manoeuvring and bringing equipment and materiel through Gornji Vakuf and Bugojno. 2. Our forces: (A) All routes and convoys have been blocked. (B) The troops are in full combat readiness. (C) There have been heavy losses and numerous civilian casualties (Croats, Muslims and Serbs) because the elementary school in the village of Rankovici in Novi Travnik municipality was hit and many apartment block are on fire. (D) At the moment, we have reliable information that the Commander of the Travnik HVO, Mr. Ivica Stojak, has been seriously wounded at the Plave Vode checkpoint. The commander of the Travnik HVO Military Police and the Assistant for SIS, Zvonko Gaso, have also been wounded, but their condition is not critical. So far, five soldiers have been killed and 20 wounded (exact data). 3. (A) Block all routes to all TO members. (B) We urgently need an intervention battalion with the strength of 150 to 200 troops on the Prozor - Bugojno - Novi Travnik and the Prozor - Bugojno - Novi Travnik axes, and the Gornji Vakuf- Novi Travnik and Bugojno - Novi Travnik roads need blocking. (C) If I do not receive reinforcements by this evening, I will be forced to withdraw units from Jajce. I therefore ask you for an urgent reply. (D) I need logistic support due to the fighting which has continued here without break since 1500 hours on 19 October 1992. (E) The Novi Travnik TO Command is in partial encirclement and retreating along the Novi Travnik - Gornji Vakuf and Novi Travnik - Ravno Rostovo - Bugojno axes. They receive support from Bugojno." Now, General, this particular document which notes that you are here, this particular document reflects that you are in Novi Travnik on the 20th of October, 1992, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. This is a report on the situation in Novi Travnik, and at 1207 hours, I was in Busovaca. I never passed the roadblock on the Busovaca-Novi Travnik road which had been erected by the BH army at Ahmici. So I could not even go to my headquarters because my headquarters was also completely surrounded. This was in Kruscica. So on the 20th of October, 1992, I was in Busovaca and not in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you say you were in Busovaca and not in Novi Travnik. Is it your testimony you never went to Novi Travnik on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I went to Novi Travnik at 0400 hours on 21 October 1992. On the 20th, I was not in Travnik at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, General.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And I was not in Travnik on either the 18th, 19th, or 20th. This is what I assert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this document, General, is it your testimony that the fighting commenced on the 18th at this gas station? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say that the incident was caused by the attempts to take over the gas station on the 18th in the evening, and then on the 18th, in the evening, the confrontation started, and there were sporadic incidents. So the very beginning, the first indications of the conflict were on the evening -- or around the 18th, but it was in the evening of the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
