utterances.text: General, in this rather detailed document that you send -- and we're talking about 644 -- in this detailed document that you sent to Boban, Stojic, and to Petkovic, you make no mention of that, do you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I mention the combat operations and the intensity of fighting as of the 19th, but I know from what I learned later that it had all started on the 18th because of the gas station and the hotel, and as for the shelling of schools, the children had gone to school that morning, this was in Rankovici in the Croatian part of Novi Travnik, and they were hit by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This incident at the gas station was the provocation that the HVO was looking for to take over Novi Travnik; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The conflict was actually a renewed conflict from June and it had to do with the old part of the hotel and the gas station, and the conflict was about who was going to control the gas station and the hotel. Now, who wanted what and how it all went at the very beginnings of this conflict, I am not familiar with, but they are the same causes as in June of 1992 except here it is clear that the preparation had been advanced on the part of the BH army because there were mortars, 120-millimetre mortars, shelling the residential areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your testimony in response to questions by my learned colleague, Mr. Nobilo, you noted that you had gone to Mostar to secure logistics and supplies for the Central Bosnian Operative Zone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I went to secure logistics for Jajce and the defenders of Jajce at the request of Stjepan Blazevic who was commander of the defence. He and the president of Jajce were desperate and they wanted me to go to Mostar to look for assistance, but I wanted to point out that the HVO from Novi Travnik only had about 30 to 50 soldiers there, so most of them were at the front lines against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. I apologise. The question concerning HVO troops in Novi Travnik was not the question on the floor. I have limited time, and I apologise for interrupting, but I must move to my next question. And the next question is this: When you went to Mostar, it was well-known, was it not, that the military commanders in the Central Bosnian Operative Zone knew that you were going down there to secure these logistics; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never told my staff, even my closest associate, where I was going. It wasn't the right thing to do when one was going. So my officer on duty obviously knew and perhaps just a very limited number of my staff, but the rest of them did not know I was going to Mostar, especially not the commanders of municipal staffs because this was a time of war, so it was -- wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, is it your testimony to this Tribunal, that you, the most senior military officer in Bosnia, did not inform anyone on your staff that you were going down to Mostar? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, he's answered the question. He said who he informed and who he didn't, and Mr. Kehoe is repeating his questions and he shouldn't be allowed to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. All right. Sustain the objection. Move to the next question, Mr. Kehoe, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your testimony is that on the 20th of October, 1992, you were not in Novi Travnik. Now, I will show you a document at this --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I say that I was not in Novi Travnik on the 20th of October, 1992, and I say that the first time I went to Novi Travnik was after a meeting with Colonel Stewart, Cumming, and Dzemo Merdan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The witness has already answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next document, Mr. President, which is a diary excerpt from Lieutenant-Colonel Robert Stewart's diary for the 20th of October, 1992. It is in English. I apologise, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 645.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're not going to blame Colonel Stewart for having written in English, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When he comes, Your Honour, you can blame him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Absolutely. You're not going to read the whole document, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Heavens no, no. The particular document that I would like to read, starting at the outset, if you could put the front page, Mr. Usher, beginning with Tuesday, 20 October. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "We had arranged to meet Tihomir Blaskic, Commander of Central Bosnia, in the Hotel Vitez at 0900 hours. But when we went into town we discovered the whole place was electric. Blaskic was not there. We cocked our weapons after some close firing by HVO soldiers in the vicinity of Hotel Vitez. They claimed to be shooting at Muslim snipers. "Mario Cerkez explained that Blaskic was in Novi Travnik where there was now serious fighting between both Croats and Muslims."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is counsel going to read the whole thing, Mr. President? The next page is Colonel Stewart going to Novi Travnik and Colonel Blaskic is not there. Could he read the whole thing, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, they're welcome to read the whole thing. My first question concerning this particular document, counsel, is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez, who is the brigade commander -- or not that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't want a dialogue to start. For the time being, the Prosecutor is indicating to the Judges, and specifically to the witness, the passages that he wants to have read. At the proper time, when you redirect, Mr. Hayman, if you find other things in the documents that you want to bring up, you can bring them up. But we are going to first hear what the witness has to say. All right. Mr. Prosecutor, concentrate on those parts of the document that you want the attention of the Judges to be called to. You're referring to Mario Cerkez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez. Mario Cerkez maintains to the commander of the British Battalion that you, General, were in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how Colonel Stewart phrased his question, Your Honours. If you were to read the entire text, Your Honours, it would be very clear, but let me repeat, I was not in Novi Travnik. This is not correct. And I can -- the only comment I can make is that I did not need to be in the Hotel Vitez because my headquarters was in Kruscica and obviously Colonel Stewart did not know that I was not to be looked for in the Hotel Vitez but, rather, in the Hotel Lovac in Kruscica, which is about 3 k from the Hotel Vitez, so I didn't even have an office in the Hotel Vitez. Next, Mario Cerkez was not the brigade commander. There was no brigade in Vitez at the time. He, at that time, was in a post of a member of the military municipal staff of HVO, and it is possible that Colonel Stewart had asked him where his commander was. But I, having given a solemn declaration here, I repeat, I was not in Novi Travnik on the 20th of October, and it is not correct that I was in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, on the 20th of October, did you order troops to pass by Ahmici and to go to Novi Travnik where they were stopped at a roadblock where, ultimately, fighting ensued?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that the fighting took place on the 20th and it started out spontaneously when the shift, which was en route to Jajce, came into conflict with those who were at the barricade at Ahmici. I don't remember having issued such a command. There could have been such an order, but I was focusing that afternoon on setting up an appointment with the main commander of the HVO. But I do not exclude the possibility that there were some conflicts at the barricade itself and in this area around the barricade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, were these troops going to Novi Travnik pursuant to your orders or were these troops going to Jajce?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If we're talking about the forces from Kiseljak, they were sent to Travnik and then on to Jajce. Those forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to a tape. I have an English translation of this tape. If I might hand this up? Mr. President, there is a reporter talking in this particular tape from Busovaca TV that is the journalist that we hear throughout.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 646.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. There is a tape that goes with this. The tape is 646 and ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, the tape is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I see that the interpreters do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We have some extra copies, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That would be good, yes. Please give it to the interpreters. Would the usher have the copies brought to the interpreters, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: To be clear, the tape is 646 and the transcript of the tape would be 646/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Is everybody ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think there is one -- one needs to go up to the booth here. If we can dim the lights and play this tape, Mr. President? If we could dim the lights, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The audio booth has an audiotape. Is that the one that you gave them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, let's hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I hope so too. It's a videotape I believe that my colleague gave to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Prosecutor. You will tell us immediately if it's not the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is this right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. (Videotape played) THE INTERPRETER (Voiceover): "Voice in the background: That is in the direction of Vitez, that is, Busovaca. After that we shall go to the village of Ahmici, where the conflict partly originated. We are just passing by the gas station. Here in the car with me are Mile, the driver, and Vlado from the intervention platoon. They have two four-barrel guns, Darko, Predrag Cunojka, up there is Vinko Petrovic and up there is Mladen Petrovic. "This is part of the route, the so-called Vitez route, and on our right is the area from which the units of the Croatian Defence Council of Vitez fired. This is part of Rovna, and on the left is the part called Hrasno. "Now we are going to the place known as Kod Picana and to the village of Ahmici. Here on the other side were some of the roadblocks set up near the cemetery. We'll stop here and film certain details. "KRISTO: Yes. You see the village of Hrasno. "Voice in the background: Yes. This is the village of Hrasno. It's alive and well ... "KRISTO: ... the Busovaca untis of the HVO... "Voice in the background: Yes, yes. The Busovaca units of the HVO fired on the village of Hrasno or from Raska Beraja. For many of those who will be watching this, here are some pictures to remember, pictures which will cause this area to be free. Here is the mosque, the upper part of which has been destroyed because there were snipers there. The units neutralised it. "KRISTO: A house. "Voice in the background : Yes. The film is from here. There, the tricolour flag is flying down there. "KRISTO: Slobodan Milosevic? "Journalist: ... keine Serbisch, Serbisch niks. Do you speak Croatian? No, Serbian, mixed Serbian. "KRISTO: Where are you from? From Jajce? "Voice in the background: Vinko, I'm coming toward you. I'm going to take you. "Journalist: Ahmici is the first and last stronghold of the Muslim armed forces. This is the point where they tried to stop members of the Croatian Defence Council who were on their way to the positions in Novi Travnik. After all the negotiations and agreements, the Muslim forces abandoned all the talks of negotiations, and the response of the Croatian Defence Council is well-known."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can bring the lights up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, that particular tape reflects that these particular soldiers were being sent to Novi Travnik, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know the soldiers, but I see that the soldiers were moving from Novi Travnik towards Busovaca. I assume that it is possible that they had been in Novi Travnik and that now they were going back --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you, General. I'm talking about the tape itself. The journalist says: "Ahmici, the first and last stronghold of the Muslim armed forces. The point where they tried to stop the members of the Croatian Defence Council who were on their way to positions in Novi Travnik. After all the negotiations and agreements, the Muslim forces abandoned all talks and negotiations, and the response of the Croatian Defence Council is well-known." According to that account, the troops that were stopped in Ahmici were headed to Novi Travnik and weren't headed to Jajce, were they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, the soldiers who had been stopped at this barricade were supposed to go to Jajce. The conflict broke out, and there was a casualty from Bilalovac. He was in the Kiseljak municipality; his name was Vidovic. They were on their way to Jajce. I know that Jajce was a difficult destination in the sense of the road. The vehicle that you saw here was of the make TAM, and the vehicle used for the transportation of soldiers to Jajce was a model 150. This is at the time when the conflict broke out. I know the soldier who died. His name is Vidovic, and I know his last name because he is a distant relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let's move to another one of your orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, what about the rest of 645?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We're not finished with it. Please, with all due respect, Mr. President, the witness has just answered questions concerning Ahmici. I am conducting the cross-examination on this particular version. Counsel has more than enough time during his redirect examination to clarify any points that he believes the Prosecutor has left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. The witness was presented with a document that's only in English. He wasn't allowed to read it; it wasn't translated for him. The rest of the document, which is Colonel Stewart's diary, describes the fact that Colonel Stewart went to Novi Travnik, that Colonel Blaskic was not there, and then later, as the witness described, there's a meeting. I think the witness should be allowed to read it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, the question has just been resolved by myself. Let us not get into a discussion. We said that in your redirect, you could ask what you like. You could say that the Prosecutor only used the parts of it that were of interest and advantage to him, which, I think, is frequently done by both parties, as you know. We are professional judges, Mr. Hayman. You will have the right, at the time you carry out your redirect, to bring out the contradictions or to criticise the method that the Prosecutor has been using in his cross-examination. But for now, the Prosecutor has the initiative to conduct his cross-examination as he pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I object to the Court being misled in that matter, only having part of the document read to it when the rest of the document absolutely confirms what the witness has said. We object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this particular point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is not the first or the second time but the last time that the Defence and the Prosecution, in the two years that this trial has been going on, when they have the initiative and when they are in charge of the proceedings, they bring out exhibits which support their thesis. First of all, after both parties have spoken, both have presented their evidence, the Judges will have to reach what ideas they have about the relevance of both sides' arguments. If the Prosecutor has only taken part of the report and if, during the cross-examination, he points out that in this or that sentence, Mario Cerkez said that Blaskic was or was not in Novi Travnik or on the next page, at line 35, it shows that Mario Cerkez says the opposite, then it will be for you to bring out the contradiction at the appropriate time, that is, during redirect, and then the Judges will withdraw from that all of the consequences. Let us not waste any further time because we have to take a break. Do you have any other questions about the cassette?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have quite a few questions around that area, Mr. President. If you want to take a break now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's a very good technique. Every time an incident occurs, I suggest that we take a 15-minute break, which allows serenity to reenter the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume the hearing now. Please be seated. Mr. Prosecutor, please resume with the document that you showed the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we move to that document, Mr. President, just referring to 645, which is the document that counsel made much ado about, we will read the pertinent portion. The document does speak for itself, but I think it's significant, given the allegations by counsel, to read this. It reads on page 23 of this diary: "At HVO headquarters, we were taken to meet Kordic. I produced Ilija and told Kordic how I came to have him with me. After that I asked if a cease-fire could be arranged."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Where are you there? Page 23, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. On the particular diary that we have, it would be the second page, the third full paragraph of that second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. Excuse me, Counsel. The document reflects a meeting between Lieutenant Colonel Stewart and Kordic in Novi Travnik. It says nothing about Blaskic being there or not being there, period, the entire insertion. It has Blaskic at a meeting later on in the day, but with regard to that time, it says nothing one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, with regard to Kordic in Novi Travnik, was he in Novi Travnik on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that he was in Novi Travnik on the 20th. But I'm underlining once again that I was not there. A few minutes ago, I heard of Colonel Stewart meeting with me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, you already said that -- you're saying that you're under oath. What is your question, Mr. Prosecutor? Let's move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next question, General, is what was Dario Kordic's role in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is hard for me to assess what his role was specifically. I was not with him, but I do know which post he held in that region. He was vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And why he went there or when he went there, he certainly didn't go there on my orders, because I did not have the power to order him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you ever together with Dario Kordic in Novi Travnik either on the 20th or the 21st of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, I was not with him. I did not even see him on the 20th of October. On the 21st, I already said that I went there at 4.00 in the morning, and in the afternoon, as I was returning from Novi Travnik, I met him. But when I was at headquarters, he was not at headquarters. I'm talking about the headquarters of the military component of the HVO in Novi Travnik at the new hotel. I was there on the 21st of October, and he was not at those headquarters at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we move to the next document, I'd like to ask you about the negotiations that took place on the afternoon of the 20th of October, 1992. You participated in those negotiations with Colonel Stewart and others, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you mean the negotiations in Vitez at the Vitez Hotel, I did take part because Colonel Stewart had sent a message asking that I take part in these meetings, and I did. By all means, I wanted that meeting with Dzemo Merdan, commander of the TO for the region of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Why did you want this meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In order to stop the combat action in Novi Travnik and to stabilise the situation and in order to help the front at Jajce and, first and foremost, to bring the conflict in Novi Travnik to a halt because I believed that I would manage to stop that with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go to another section of Colonel Stewart's diary on that day, and this is the last page of that three-page diary, Your Honour, about midway through, where Colonel Stewart writes as follows: "Blaskic, who represented the HVO, was adamant that the Territorial Defence force should unconditionally surrender. In particular though they must surrender their weapons, come under HVO control and give Lendo to the HVO as well. After about 45 minutes Andrew Cumming joined us. We were getting nowhere when Andrew suggested a harder line. He suggested that the Territorial Defence force should remove Lendo. But it also emerged that the HVO Representative had written instructions not to compromise." General, did you demand that the Territorial Defence come under the control of the HVO, and did you have instructions from your superiors not to compromise?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I must say that the environment in which the meeting took place -- I think I should describe that, and then it would be clearer what I asked for. Captain Nick interpreted at the meeting. He had a very poor understanding of the Croat language. At that meeting, two bottles of whiskey were consumed. I don't know how come it doesn't say so there. Dzemo and I don't drink alcohol at all. The meeting went on from 23.00 until 03.00, and Dzemo spoke at this meeting saying that he was being asked that the Territorial Defence hand over its weapons to the HVO. In relation to that, I said to Dzemo Merdan that that was not true. I said, "Dzemo, that is not true. That is not the position of the HVO. Tell me who presented that position before you? I'm telling you now that that's not what the HVO is asking for. The HVO does not need weapons and the HVO is not asking for weapons from the Territorial Defence in Novi Travnik." I did ask for Commander Lendo to be handed over because I considered him to be responsible for the killing of the commander of the HVO in Travnik, the one who was killed at the checkpoint of -- rather, at the roadblock of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and his deputy was heavily wounded there and they were from Travnik, and when Brigadier Cumming, at around 2.30 a.m., he asked for Dzemo Merdan to replace Commander Lendo from his position, we agreed on that and we parted on that and we said that we would continue our talks but that this should all take place as soon as possible. After the meeting, I left immediately during that night, and I arrived in Novi Travnik at 4.00 in the morning of the 21st of October; and at headquarters in the new hotel at Novi Travnik, I conveyed this to the commander, that is, everything that we had agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your testimony is that this meeting that you attended with Bob Stewart and others was conducted, at least on your end, in a spirit of conciliation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said what this meeting was like and I said that I openly stated to Mr. Dzemo Merdan at this meeting that no one from the HVO, I'm talking about the command that was under my command, that the TO surrender its arms and that no one was asking for the TO to surrender to the HVO; but at the outset, the position was as follows, that I had asked for the TO to hand over Commander Lendo because of everything that had happened that day and during that conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, approximately what time will we be going to this evening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Until 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, General, if I can?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 647, 647A for the French version and 647B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, take a look at this report. This is your report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would you have a copy for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this is your report to all HVO municipal headquarters dated 21 October, 1992, at 2100 hours. Now, before we read through this, which we will do, General, I ask you to go back and take a look at the last paragraph on this document, document 10 -- excuse me, paragraph 10, I'm sorry, paragraph 10 of this document, which notes: "While defence operations are being conducted, the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna Dario Kordic and I are in Novi Travnik, continuously leading the military operations with deep knowledge of the situation and by keeping all the forces under control. Commander of the Operations Group Colonel Filip Filipovic is also here and the Novi Travnik HVO HQ." So, General, when you told us a couple of minutes ago that you weren't in Novi Travnik with Dario Kordic, you weren't telling us the truth, were you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You asked me about the 20th of October, whether I was with Dario Kordic. On the 21st, I said that I met Dario Kordic, but I did not find him at headquarters in the morning at 4.00 when I was at headquarters of the municipal staff of Novi Travnik at the new hotel. He was not there. But I did say that I saw him later during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, General, where were you continuously leading the military operations with Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This report was written at 2100 hours on the 21st of October, and I would have to study this document, to read this document, it has two pages, and I should see what it's all about. But I still claim that on the 21st, in the morning, at headquarters in the hotel in Novi Travnik, I did not see Dario Kordic, and at that time, he was not at the hotel when I was there. But I did see him on the 21st in Novi Travnik but at another place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, General, this document is dated 2100 hours, 9.00 at night, so when you told us that you left Novi Travnik at noontime on the 21st, that wasn't true either, was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I returned to the Hotel Lovac in order to prepare, on the 21st of October, Mr. Marko Prskalo, who was supposed to be president of the commission, and later he was, for implementing the agreement on the cease-fire in Novi Travnik and on looking into the causes of the conflict. I gave him instructions and later I probably went to Novi Travnik from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You did not ask me. You are asking me now whether it is correct that I left Novi Travnik and whether I went to Vitez, and I'm saying, yes, I did do that in order to meet with Marko Prskalo, an officer from my command, so that I would agree on these things with him related to the agreement on the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, during the course of your direct questioning by Mr. Nobilo, did you tell the Court that you had, in fact, been involved in Novi Travnik during combat operations on the 21st of October of 1992? Did you tell the Judges that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that I arrived in Novi Travnik on the 21st at 4.00, and now I should look at the rest to see what are the other details that I spoke of, but I concentrated on the most important segments of my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think the record will reflect itself, Mr. President, that the witness made no commentary about his activities in Novi Travnik on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us read this document, General.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. On the 21st of October, I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this method is also unacceptable. The witness did not speak about many things during the examination-in-chief because we were in a hurry. We thought that we should make a selection of relevant and irrelevant things. That's what you asked for. First of all, the conflict in Novi Travnik is not part of the indictment, and the witness did say something about it but we did not go into details because it was not in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's be careful here. I don't want it to say in the transcript that it was pursuant to instructions from the Trial Chamber that the parties did not judge that it was essential to call attention to relevant things. I want to make it clear on behalf of my colleagues that you choose your own strategy, and let me remind you that there are always time constraints for which we are responsible pursuant to several Rules, especially Rule 90(G). Don't put any words in my mouth that I never said. I'm just speaking about time constraints, but within the time constraints, everyone is free to act according to his own strategy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, Novi Travnik is part of the indictment in Count 1 of the indictment, and with regard to the Novi Travnik issues itself, Blaskic begins to talk about Novi Travnik commencing on page 8007 and then continues to talk about it for 45 pages of the transcript. Let us look at this document, General. Excuse me. I have been corrected by my colleague, Mr. President. The issue of Novi Travnik comes up in paragraph 5.2 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us look at this document, General, dated the 21st of October, 1992, at 2100 hours, your announcement or report on the situation in Novi Travnik and Jajce. "1. SITUATION AT THE NOVI TRAVNIK FRONT: "(a) Muslim forces continue intensive artillery operations aimed at the town itself and operate generally using 122 mm howitzers. The most fortified positions of the Muslim forces are the village of Opara where the command is based, Kasapovici, the village of Isakovici south of 612 by 500, the village of Vejzovici, Sinokos, Senkovici, and Turalici. The enemy has disarmed HVO units in villages inhabited by an unknown number of Croatian people. Some Croats have been taken prisoner in the villages of Kopilo, Torine, Senkovici, and Bugojcici." Moving down towards the end of that paragraph: "The enemy is attempting to plant misinformation about alleged successes of its forces which is a downright lie and certainly has a counterproductive effect on its units. "The loudspeaker of the mosque in the village of Ahmici, Vitez Municipality, was used to call upon the Croatian people to hand over their weapons. "(b) HVO UNITS: "1. All roads to the town of Novi Travnik have been blocked and no access will be granted to the town without our permission for the time being, after 1945 hours. In other words, the town is under a complete blockade. "2. The blockade of all roads was lifted along with singing of the songs Cavoglava ... and Evo zore, evo dana. The amplified singing shook the town. Muslim forces were pushed back towards the villages with a majority of Muslim inhabitants. The villages of Kasapovici, Isakovici, and Lasine were completely blocked and exposed to intense firing from our forces. "3. The situation in Travnik, Zenica, Vitez, Busovaca, Kiseljak, Fojnica, Kresevo, Vares, and Kakanj is under complete control of the HVO, but the behaviour of the HVO military and civilian personnel in Travnik was incomprehensible. They began negotiations and arrangements for a cease-fire after the assassination of the commander of the Travnik Command HQ, the late Ivica Stojak, without the knowledge of their superior command and taking advantage of our preoccupation of the situation in Novi Travnik and Vitez. "4. Tensions are really high in Travnik and Zenica, but it was made clear to the Muslim forces that our units will prevent any movement of the Territorial Defence towards Novi Travnik and therefore the units are currently passive. "5. The barricade on the Busovaca - Vitez main road, in the village of Ahmici, Vitez Municipality, was completely destroyed and the Muslim forces were driven out of the village and crushed entirely. The Muslim forces also surrendered their weapons on their own initiative. In Ahmici, the mosque was used for military purposes (with the loudspeaker to call on HVO defenders to surrender weapons). As a result, fire was opened on the tower. Since yesterday, the village is under full control of the HVO." Let us move to the last sentence in paragraph 6. "6. The activities of our forces are organised, fully coordinated and controlled by the command. "8. Casualties on our side: (A) 10 dead (b) 32 wounded (c) 5 known to be missing. Casualties on the Muslim side are unknown since they do not transport their wounded to the Travnik hospital but we saw them transporting the dead on two tractors. Many have been taken prisoner. "9. The additional personnel I had asked for will NOT BE REQUIRED FOR NOW since the situation in all the municipalities is under control. The road from Gornji Vakuf to Novi Travnik has been blocked by forces of the Fojnica Municipal HQ and the Bugojno - Novi Travnik road by the Bugojno HVO forces. The personnel which was sent by you and which has reached Prozor (according to our sources) may remain there temporarily or return. We have irrefutable proof that the mosque towers are being used as shelters by snipers. Whenever we launch any operations against them, they identify us as Chetniks. "10. While defence operations are being conducted, the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna Dario Kordic and I are in Novi Travnik, continuously leading the military operations with deep knowledge of the situation and by keeping all the forces under control. Commander of the Operative Group Colonel Filip Filipovic is also here and the Novi Travnik HVO HQ. "The misinformation about any of our commanders being taken prisoner persistently being spread by the so-called 'Supreme Command of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army' is incorrect, since UN vehicles must be secured for the transfer of their commander of the District HQ of the Zenica TO to their zone of responsibility." This document, of course, is signed by you as commander of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone and also by Dario Kordic. General, this is your document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is my document, on the 21st of October at 21.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, it is clear that on the 21st of October, the HVO is in control of virtually all of Central Bosnia, and read paragraph 3: "Travnik, Zenica, Vitez, Busovaca, Kiseljak, Fojnica, Kresevo, Vares, and Kakanj," they're all under your control?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was no conflict there and only HVO members are under the control of the command, and Travnik cannot be under HVO control when there is the TO there too, and at that time the Mujahedin too and members of other units or, I don't know, Zenica. In Zenica is the headquarters of the 3rd Corps, and the 3rd Corps is not under my command, and all the forces of the 3rd Corps. And you also mentioned Vitez. In Vitez, the 325th Brigade is not under my command; in Busovaca the 333rd Brigade is not under my control; in Kiseljak, the 310th Brigade is not under my control; and so on and so forth. In Fojnica, the BH army forces are not under my control; in Kresevo, in Vares and Kakanj; but the HVO forces are under my control. Because it says "the situation," that is to say, the state of affairs there; it doesn't say that the area is under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, did you write this document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know why this part was omitted in terms of treatment of the wounded. In this situation, we did not have a hospital either. I don't know why you omitted that, but the document does speak about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Try to focus on the question that was asked. That will help us to understand things better. Mr. Kehoe, you asked a question about paragraph 3 regarding the sentence about areas under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the dominant military force in all of these municipalities was the Croatian Defence Council, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, at that time, Zenica had a population of 100.000 Muslim Bosniaks, I mean, and perhaps only 20.000 Croats. What are these dominant forces of the HVO in Zenica as related to the TO? I'm referring to the situation that was under control in terms of the soldiers, that is to say, that there was no escalation of the conflict in Zenica. There wasn't. There wasn't in Kakanj and elsewhere too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, I think we've got to move to another question. You're asking us the questions when you're the one that's supposed to answer. You're not a neutral observer here, but, rather, a privileged witness. Otherwise, I think we have to move to another question, and your answer has been indicated in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, the town of Travnik had a tradition of conciliation and ethnic brotherhood between the Croats and the Muslims, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not only the town of Travnik but the entire region before these problems and incidents. Not only Travnik. Travnik was not special in that regard with respect to the other parts, areas. It was a similar situation in Kiseljak and other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yet you, General, just told us that you came to the meeting on the 20th with Colonel Stewart in the spirit of conciliation, but in this document you are outraged that Travnik has entered into a cease-fire with the Muslims, and that's in paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is right, but if you look at the further history of these ceasefires, you will see what took place, but this document, 647, when you describe the situation under (a), you have the "intensive artillery operations at the town itself ... using 122 mm howitzers" were continued. They were fired against residential areas. I came in a conciliatory mode, but things were not going in that direction. Later on, the minister had to intervene in order that we reached a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, the HVO had completely blockaded the town of Novi Travnik, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It blocked all the access roads which it could in order to localise this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Also, in paragraph 9, the HVO controlled the roads from Gornji Vakuf to Novi Travnik and from Bugojno to Novi Travnik; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, yes, the HVO had erected barricades on those roads from Novi Travnik to Gornji Vakuf, and the barricade from Bugojno to Novi Travnik was erected by the Bugojno HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, when you were at the model and you were showing us all the places where the Bosnians had checkpoints and control, you never told us that in October of 1992, the HVO had control of all the access roads between Novi Travnik and Gornji Vakuf and Novi Travnik and Bugojno, did you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had stated to this Trial Chamber when the attack on Medenik happened, that is, on the Novi Travnik-Gornji Vakuf road in '93, and the BH army had broken up and dispersed the HVO troops and taken control of this road, I said that the BH army had deployed 200 soldiers at the Vora Vode school in Novi Travnik, that they put Mujahedins in Rostovo on the Novi Travnik-Bugojno road and that through these operations, it was assuming control over the roads. At Medenik, the HVO had held these positions, and the BH army attacked it in January. I believe it was on 14 January, 1993. I think it is in my testimony somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, did you tell the Chamber that by the 21st of October, 1992, the HVO was in full control of all access roads going to Novi Travnik from Bugojno and Gornji Vakuf? Did you tell the Trial Chamber that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Objection as to form, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, we heard days and days and hours of testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Rephrase your question. Rephrase your question, please. Make it specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you testify, in response to questions by Mr. Nobilo, that the HVO controlled all the access roads into Central Bosnia through Novi Travnik on the 21st of October? Did you tell the Court that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Take your time. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I either did not understand the question or something was wrong with the interpretation. Could you please just repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During your answers to questions by Mr. Nobilo in direct examination, did you tell the Trial Chamber that on the 21st of October, the HVO had full control over the roads through Novi Travnik, from Bugojno to Novi Travnik and Gornji Vakuf to Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, here's the problem. Counsel could repeat the question for every day of the war. "Did you tell the Court that on the 18th of July you controlled this road or you didn't?" It's an objection as to form. If counsel believes that the witness misled the Court, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, your client is the one who didn't understand the question. Therefore, don't jump up with all the excitement that you display. It's simply that General Blaskic asked that the question be repeated. I think that we can wait for the witness to answer. Take your time. Think about it if you need to.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not speak of all the details because I focused on what was the most important. As regards the control, this situation is presented here based on the reports which I had received and which were in force on the 21st maybe through the 25th of October. But I explained how the operations developed and how all these roads in the course of time came under the control of the BH army. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, please, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's move to paragraph 5, General, where you noted that with regard to the village of Ahmici, the barricade was completely destroyed and that the Muslim forces were driven out of the village and crushed entirely; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the Busovaca highway, and it is correct that the barricade had been destroyed and that the Muslim forces were driven out and crushed. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you told the Court on page 18012 that the barricade had been dismantled, what actually happened was significantly more violent; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was fighting over the barricade, and I know that the barricade was removed under fighting. I don't know exactly what I stated, I would have to look at it, but there was some fighting going on around the barricade, and that was the circumstances under which it was removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We don't know whether it was crushed, whether it was diminished, whether -- let's move on. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In paragraph 5, you say it was crushed entirely. In your testimony, you note that this barricade was dismantled. My question for you is that what you write in this report, that it was completely destroyed, is significantly more violent than just dismantling the barricade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, let's show the witness his testimony if we're going to engage in this. He stated at page 18013 that people were killed, there was a death on the Croatian side, a death on the Bosnian side, and that structures were burned. That's in his testimony to this Court on direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There were Muslim houses too that were burnt. Muslim houses were burnt. What he said with regard to this particular barricade as opposed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm going to speak on behalf of the Judges. I'll ask the question; otherwise, we're never going to move forward at all. General Blaskic, when you write in paragraph 5 that the roadblock was completely destroyed and that the Muslim forces, who had to take people out of the village, were completely crushed, was that your sentence?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can confirm this sentence, and when I talked about the conflict in Ahmici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation obscured] ... the Judges, they have texts in front of them, and they can distinguish the difference between "completely destroyed" and "completely crushed." We understand the difference between "crushed" and "destroyed." Let's move to another question. It's now ten to six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, it's also true, is it not, that the Muslim forces in Ahmici surrendered their weapons voluntarily? Paragraph 5, second full sentence.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The sentence reads that they surrendered their weapons on their own initiative in Ahmici. They don't say how many there were, just the forces who did so in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that true?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the report that I had received, and I consider it correct, that I received it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you also note that at this juncture, on the 21st of October, 1992, in this last sentence at paragraph 6, "The activities of our forces are organised, fully coordinated, and controlled by the command." By that statement, General, in October of 1992, you are noting that command and control is operating, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the information at my disposal at the time, I believed that this was so, in other words, that the activities had been coordinated, and this is how I stated it. I stated it as I believed it to be at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, once again, at paragraph 10, General, when you note that you and Kordic are in Novi Travnik continuously leading military operations, I ask you, what was Dario Kordic's role in leading these military operations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I say this, I am referring to the disinformation that we had both been captured by the Muslim forces. That information was disseminated in the media. It was true that the commander from Travnik had been killed, but there was this disinformation. I already stated what his duty was. He was the deputy president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What was Dario Kordic doing in leading the military operation? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dario Kordic, together with -- was with the civilian authorities, that is, with the municipal government of the HVO, the president and other officials. I did not directly communicate with him; I don't know what duties they had at the time. But I know that the problem we had at the time was that we could not reach the hospital in Travnik, so I believe that he was involved in trying to find a solution for the wounded because we had been cut off, and our access to the hospital was cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you saw him in Novi Travnik, was he wearing a uniform? I'm talking about Dario Kordic now.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The whole time, I think, until the Dayton Accord was signed, he was wearing a uniform. In fact, I don't know that I ever saw him not wearing a uniform in Central Bosnia. He may have not worn one, but he usually wore it, just like all the other officials at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who was he with when you saw him in Novi Travnik on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was mostly the officials of the civilian authorities, so it would be the president of the HVO, vice-president. One's name was Jozo; I think his last name was Sekic. Another one was called Marinko. Then the head of defence for civilian defence in Novi Travnik and other officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, when you met in Novi Travnik on the 21st, what did you talk about, you and Kordic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed them on what agreement we had reached with Merdan and what I had expected of the TO and what else we should do in order to stabilise this cease-fire. So that was the direction that the discussion took.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, the bottom line is, did he or did he not lead military operations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I was there, I am sure that he was not, and I came on 21 October, '92. Whether anything happened before I arrived or afterwards, because I left on the 22nd to Kiseljak, the 23rd to Kiseljak, I do not know what he did specifically. But when I was there, he did not lead any military operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you write in the report that you and Kordic were leading military operations, you don't know of any military operations that Kordic led; is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say what I have just stated, that when I was there, I know and I'm convinced that he did nothing in terms of military affairs, and this is my submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then why did you put that in the report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was referring to myself, that I personally was leading the operations and conducting them while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. General, the document says very clearly: "The vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and I are in Novi Travnik continuously leading the military operations."

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already stated what issues he was dealing with, and what I did, for the most part, was in reference to the information that we had both been captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't think you're really answering the question, General Blaskic. Either we're not going to have that question answered or something else. "Dario Kordic and I remained in Novi Travnik," we knew all about that question, "and we were aware of all the forces under our control." Keep the answer the same as what you had given. It only involves yourself.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, when I was there, I did command, and control and command involves and leadership also involves other issues like organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you're the one who wrote this, General Blaskic. We're not the ones who are giving answers. We're asking you to help us. The Prosecutor is asking, when you say that "Dario Kordic and myself will stay here in order to continuously direct military operations," you're not talking about civilian operations. You're the one who wrote that. I can't answer for you. You're the only one who can answer. Say that you don't know or you can't remember or that it doesn't match the actual facts. I don't know. All of us are trying to understand things here. I think that Judge Shahabuddeen also wishes to ask a question, as well as Judge Rodrigues. What is your last answer in respect of this question, this point, this very specific point, when you write this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I state that I am leading military operations, I am saying that I am commanding the military operations. For instance, there was also an issue of caring for the wounded, and he was dealing with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't think we can go any further than that. That's your answer. That's your right. That's the witness's right. Do you have another question before I give the floor to Judge Shahabuddeen in respect of the various aspects of this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you still have any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me turn to Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, this report is dated the 21st of October, 1992, that is, some seven months before the events which occurred at Ahmici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 5 and, in particular, the last sentence. You state there: "Since yesterday, the village," I take it that refers to Ahmici, "is under full control of the HVO." Did the BiH army ever subsequently dislodge the HVO from the position of full control of Ahmici which it had acquired on 20th October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In Ahmici was the 3rd company of the 325th Mountain Brigade of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from Vitez. Then on the slopes behind Ahmici was the position of these forces, that is to say, that this was the situation probably in October. The command of that company was in the elementary school in Ahmici. Cooperation between the HVO in the area of Vitez, like in other municipalities, was dynamic. It varied. For a certain period of time, it would be very good. For example, after the conflict, we had very good cooperation, and then there were incidents, and then it would repeat itself. That is what life was like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What I'm trying to clear my mind on is this: On the 20th of October, 1992, the HVO, so you say, had acquired full control of Ahmici. I'm asking whether the HVO lost that control or terminated that control later on or was dislodged by the BiH army later on? Can you answer that as clearly as you can?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that the most precise way of putting it is that this control stopped when the cease-fire agreement came into being, and when the commission was set up by the Minister of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it was set up for implementing all agreements relating to the joint command, and the TO or, rather, the BH army was no longer in the focus of attention, and we focused on the front line and on the Serbs together and together we reconstructed various facilities in Ahmici, so this was stabilised at local level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: When was this cease-fire agreement?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This general agreement at the highest level was around the 3rd of November, 1992, and the local agreement was between the 20th and the 25th, in that period, the 20th and the 25th of October in 1992, and at that time, the joint commission was set up as well which was supposed to ascertain the causes of the conflict in Novi Travnik. However, this joint commission stopped working because the Muslim officials no longer participated in this commission as of the 4th of November in 1992. The killers of Commander Stojak were supposed to be handed over and also the protagonists of the conflict in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm only asking, General, whether the HVO continued in control or lost control. I think I've got the answer from what you've said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me remind you that tomorrow we have a day from 10.00 to 1.00 and then from 2.30 to 5.30. The same thing on Wednesday. On Thursday, we will meet from 9.00 to 1.30, and we will not sit in the afternoon nor on Friday morning. All right. Court stands adjourned. We will resume tomorrow at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 6.07 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of May, 1999, at 10.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
